title: Observability: OTel GenAI Spans and Prometheus Metrics

questions.question: Before reading the lesson: what is the practical benefit of writing your harness's spans in the OTel GenAI attribute shape?
options: OTel spans compress noticeably better on disk than an equivalent ad hoc JSON log format
OTel is a Python-only standard, so adopting it gives the harness static type hints for free
Emitting spans in the OTel GenAI shape is required for HIPAA compliance in a healthcare deployment
Every OTel-compatible backend, from Honeycomb to Datadog, can read them without a custom parser
questions.explanation: The conventions are a contract with the wider ecosystem. Honeycomb, Grafana Tempo, Jaeger, and Datadog all parse gen_ai.* attributes out of the box — compression, typing, and compliance are not the reason.

questions.question: An exception is raised inside a SpanBuilder.span() context. What does the lesson's builder record?
options: status=ERROR, status_message includes the exception type and message, and an 'exception' event is appended.
The span is dropped entirely before being written to traces.jsonl, to avoid polluting the trace with failures
status remains UNSET, and the exception is caught and silently swallowed without being re-raised
The span's name field is rewritten to 'error' in place of its original operation name
questions.explanation: Status ERROR plus an exception event matches the OTel spec. The exception is re-raised so caller code can react — the span is not dropped, swallowed, or renamed.

questions.question: The Prometheus exposition for a histogram includes _bucket, _sum, and _count lines. Why are bucket counts cumulative (each le bucket includes all smaller buckets)?
options: Cumulative bucket counts are the only histogram format that the Grafana dashboarding tool is able to render
The lesson's histogram exposition is actually non-standard; real Prometheus histograms are not cumulative at all
Cumulative counts let the scraper compute per-bucket counts via subtraction without storing all observations.
Cumulative counts reduce the floating-point rounding error that would otherwise accumulate across many buckets
questions.explanation: Prometheus' design choice: a backend reads cumulative counts and computes per-bucket differences. This lets the time series be a simple monotonic counter per bucket — it is standard behavior, not a Grafana requirement or a precision trick.

questions.question: The harness wraps a tool execution in a span. Which attribute keys identify it as a tool call under the GenAI conventions?
options: gen_ai.system and gen_ai.request.model, the pair used to identify which provider and model handled a chat span
gen_ai.tool.name and gen_ai.tool.call.id, the canonical keys for tool executions in the GenAI conventions
agent.harness.tool and agent.harness.call, a harness-local naming scheme instead of the standardized GenAI keys
operation and tool.name, a shorthand pair that is not part of the GenAI semantic conventions at all
questions.explanation: gen_ai.tool.name and gen_ai.tool.call.id are the canonical keys for tool executions in the GenAI conventions; the other pairs either identify a chat span or aren't part of the standard at all.

questions.question: You want to query 'what is the p95 latency of read_file calls'. Which artifact do you query?
options: The Prometheus histogram tool_latency_ms{tool="read_file"}, scraped and used to derive the percentile
Each span's duration_ms field inside traces.jsonl, extracted and aggregated by a one-off parsing script
The counter tools_called_total, divided by the length of the observation time window in seconds
The status_message field of the span, which records human-readable detail about how the call ended
questions.explanation: Histograms are the right tool for percentiles. The counter only counts; the trace contains raw spans but is not pre-aggregated, and status_message is unrelated to latency.

questions.question: A reviewer asks why the lesson hand-rolls instead of importing opentelemetry-sdk. Which answer is correct?
options: The official opentelemetry-sdk package does not support the GenAI semantic conventions at all
Hand-rolling the span builder produces measurably faster code at runtime than the official SDK
Importing opentelemetry-sdk requires an active network connection at import time, which breaks offline use
Hand-rolling teaches the wire format directly; production can drop in the SDK later, reusing the same gen_ai.* keys
questions.explanation: The conventions are stable across implementations. The hand-rolled version exists for clarity; production wires in the SDK and reuses the same gen_ai.* keys — the SDK supports GenAI conventions fine and needs no network access to import.
